unit.title: Ratios, Rates, and Linear Relationships
unit.act: Act IV - Turning constant change into lines
unit.role: Connect proportional reasoning, slope, equations, graphs, and linear models.
unit.governingQuestion: How do two quantities change together at a constant rate?
unit.storyArc: Ratios become unit rates, proportionality becomes a line through the origin, and slope generalizes constant rate. Multiple line forms reveal different information; data modeling distinguishes exact relationships from approximate trends.
outcomes: Use ratios, unit rates, proportions, and percent multipliers.
Interpret a graph as a set of ordered-pair solutions.
Calculate and interpret intercepts and slope with units.
Write line equations from points, graphs, and contexts.
Fit, interpret, and critique elementary linear models.
unit.investigation: Analyze a real cost, consumption, or public-data set and defend a linear model with a reasonable domain and limitations.
unit.mastery: Students move among context, table, graph, and formula and explain slope and intercept with units.
